DW-22.intent: Give the headless host a bounded exec path so the declared debug_exec timeout is real: run the exec body on a worker thread and have Marshal.call's existing done.wait(timeout_s) actually block, so exceeding the budget returns a TIMEOUT envelope instead of hanging the server. Because a Python thread cannot be forcibly killed, the abandoned body may still be running, so the timeout must mark the session document-suspect exactly as MarshalTimeout's docstring specifies (no blind retry) and the TIMEOUT envelope must say so. Keep the GUI/RPC host's marshal semantics unchanged, and add an external test that a sleeping/looping exec body yields TIMEOUT rather than blocking.
DW-22.label: Thread-based bounded exec

Also make the after line carry the call result rather than repeating the pre-execution params, so an audit pair records what changed instead of the same input twice. Fail the audit open rather than failing the tool call when a handle cannot be resolved, keep the GUI/RPC path's audit semantics identical to the MCP path, and add an external test asserting a mutation's audit pair carries two differing non-null fingerprints and a result-bearing after payload.
DW-24.label: Thread the registry now
